text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore's Pepole's Action Party says they have no plans to use changes to the electoral boundaries as tactics to defeat the opposition.
- U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher in Israel to urge Israelis and Palestinians to reach swift and significant results in peace talks.
- Soaring Dow Jones Industrial Average is likely to divert U.S. funds into undervalued markets in Asia.
- Two prominent Wall Street bears start sprouting bullish horns in the face of recent stock market record and bond market rally.
- Jurong Town Corp intends to sub-lease Pulau Merlimau to Singapore Refining Company for building of oil handling dock and a dry dock.
- Hongkong firms scurry to list spinoffs on overseas markets.
- Foreign banks are getting wary about lending money to the Thai market and some banks have been asked to submit reports about their loan exposure to Thailand.
- Head of World Bank mission says China's growth is declining, inflation is above official figures and state industry is in dire straits.
- Diversified Sime Singapore expcts property to be its main engine of growth.
- Technochem, a subsidiary of Sime Singapore, is investing Singapore $3 million in a new chemical incinerator that destroys toxic wastes.
